## What I did

Created **`src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFormatAgentTest.java`** (only that file), a JUnit 4 test class matching the existing `CSVFormatTest` style: `org.junit.Test`, static `org.junit.Assert.*` imports, `@Test(expected = …)` for error cases, and a private `assertNotEquals` helper mirroring the existing one.

### Coverage (90 test methods, public API only)

| Area | Happy path | Boundary / error |
|---|---|---|
| Predefined constants (`DEFAULT`, `RFC4180`, `EXCEL`, `MYSQL`, `TDF`, `INFORMIX_UNLOAD*`) | assert every getter value (delimiter, quote, escape, null string, record separator, flags) | — |
| `Predefined` enum + `valueOf` | `getFormat()` returns the exact static instance | `valueOf("unknown")` → `IllegalArgumentException` |
| `newFormat(char)` | all other fields null/false | `'\n'` / `'\r'` delimiter → `IllegalArgumentException` |
| `withXxx` builders | returned value + **immutability of the original** + chaining; disable-by-`null` for quote/comment/escape/nullString; boolean toggles both directions | line-break chars, delimiter == quote/escape/comment, quote == comment, escape == comment, `QuoteMode.NONE` without escape, duplicate header entries — all throw |
| Header | input/output array copy semantics (mutating either side doesn't leak), `withHeader()` empty vs `null`, enum / empty-enum / null-enum / null-`ResultSet`, `withFirstRecordAsHeader`, header-comment stringification + defensive copy | — |
| `equals` / `hashCode` | reflexive, equal formats share hashCode, `equalWhenBothHaveNoQuote` | rejects `null` & foreign types; unequal on delimiter, quote char, header order, record separator, null string, one-sided quote |
| `toString` | contains `Delimiter=<,>`, `QuoteChar`, `RecordSeparator`, optional `CommentStart`/`Escape`/`NullString`/`Header` sections | absent sections not printed |
| `format(Object...)` | empty, simple, quoting a delimiter-bearing value, custom delimiter, `QuoteMode.ALL` / `NON_NUMERIC`, null→empty vs null-string | null emitted verbatim (not escaped) even with an escape char set — the Csv-14 concern |
| `print` / `println` / `printRecord` (Appendable) | first-field vs delimiter-prefixed, quote doubling, null-string, trim effect, record separator, trailing delimiter, `print(Appendable)` returns a working `CSVPrinter` | — |
| `parse(Reader)` | multi-record read with positional access, header-name access, `withIgnoreSurroundingSpaces` strips spaces | empty input → no records |
